notable_absence.finding: Before this record, the registry's server: namespace held only architectural nouns (node, rebalance, multi-dimensional-scaling, service-memory-quota) and had nothing at all for the basic item/key/value/document primitives that every n1ql:*, sdk:* and eventing:* concept ultimately reads or writes. Nine-plus rounds of reference-page extraction from statement and privilege pages never surfaced these because those pages assume the data model rather than stating it - it took this conceptual page to state it in the docs' own words.

cross_component_finding: The page's Sub-Documents section ties the document/attribute/sub-document path model directly to the SDK's Sub-Document API ('The Couchbase SDK provides a _Sub-Document API_, which allows paths to be specified, and sub-documents thereby read and written to'), i.e. to the already-promoted sdk:subdocument-operations. But no page anywhere in the registry states whether that same path syntax is the one n1ql:select and n1ql:update use to project or set individual document fields in SQL++ - the two addressing schemes read as the same idea (dot/bracket paths into a JSON document) but the identity is never asserted on any page read so far, so it is left as an open question rather than merged.
cross_product_finding: This page's data:document (a JSON value stored and served by Couchbase Server's Data service) shares its exact name with the already-promoted sgw:document (Sync Gateway's sync-function processing unit, a different product). Per the registry's existing collision-tracking convention (capella:cluster-manager vs capella-role:cluster-manager, the four-way 'role' split), the two are kept as separate ids here rather than merged - no page read in this batch states a relationship between Couchbase Server's document and Sync Gateway's document, so asserting one would be inventing a fact, not extracting one.
